clinical_summary: Capecitabine is chemotherapy taken as tablets. NCCP 00216 covers several colorectal and breast cancer settings, including treatment after surgery and treatment of advanced disease. Ask which aim and duration apply to you.
component_rationale: After you swallow capecitabine, your body changes it into fluorouracil. This interferes with the DNA and RNA processes cells use to grow. Normal cells can also be affected, which helps explain mouth soreness, bowel symptoms and changes in blood counts.
schedule_context: capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Follow your individual prescription.
key_points: Current toxicity and recurrence guide different decisions
Confirm colorectal versus breast indication before interpreting evidence

treatment_rationale.summary: Capecitabine is chemotherapy taken as tablets. NCCP 00216 covers several colorectal and breast cancer settings, including treatment after surgery and treatment of advanced disease. Ask which aim and duration apply to you.
treatment_rationale.setting: Breast and colorectal cancer indications; 1250 mg/m² twice daily on days 1–14 every 21 days.
treatment_rationale.line: Confirm the exact NCCP indication and previous treatment; shared indications do not have a single line of therapy.
factors: Previous therapy, organ function and DPD status
Toxicity, practical burden and patient preference
alternatives: Discuss indication-specific systemic options, treatment modification and supportive care with the treating team.
limitations: In stage III colon cancer after surgery, capecitabine was at least as effective as the intravenous fluorouracil schedule studied. This comparison does not measure benefit against no treatment, and does not estimate benefit for breast cancer or cancer that has spread.
Trial results describe groups and cannot predict an individual outcome. The official regimen determines eligibility and dosing.

patient_selection.treatment_intent: Capecitabine is chemotherapy taken as tablets. NCCP 00216 covers several colorectal and breast cancer settings, including treatment after surgery and treatment of advanced disease. Ask which aim and duration apply to you.
disease_and_biomarker_context: Use the exact NCCP indication; DPD testing is a safety assessment, not a tumour biomarker.
For colorectal disease, systemic choices also depend on the MDT plan, disease setting and molecular work-up.
eligibility_orientation: Assess counts, renal/hepatic function, symptoms and safe oral administration.
important_cautions: Complete DPD deficiency, severe prior fluoropyrimidine reaction, relevant hypersensitivity and pregnancy/lactation are exclusions.
Brivudine requires avoidance and an interval of at least four weeks before capecitabine.
The renal table differs between 00623 and 00216/00586; do not transplant dose rules.

supportive_care.emetogenic_risk: Capecitabine · active treatment cycle: Oral minimal-to-low
premedication_and_prophylaxis: The team agrees a rescue medicine if needed; routine daily anti-sickness prevention is not automatically required for this oral low-risk schedule.
Report diarrhoea promptly and follow the written rescue plan. Severe symptoms, fever, dehydration or inability to drink need urgent advice.
White-cell growth-factor injections are prescribed according to individual risk and previous complications. They are not automatically required for every patient or every cycle.
Use gentle skin and mouth care. Painful hands and feet or mouth sores can require a tablet hold and team review; do not continue simply to finish the pack.

Where prescribed under the capecitabine source: loperamide 4 mg initially then 2 mg after each loose stool, maximum 16 mg/day; follow the written local escalation plan. Do not copy the irinotecan high-dose schedule.

baseline: Full blood count, kidney and liver profile before starting.
Confirm DPD testing before the first fluoropyrimidine dose unless already tested; review renal impairment when interpreting uracil phenotyping.
Review cardiac history; ECG when cardiac function is compromised or clinical findings warrant it. No automatic serial echocardiogram schedule is specified for this regimen.
before_each_cycle: Full blood count, kidney and liver profile before each cycle.
Review current and worst symptoms since the previous dose, oral intake, hydration, mouth soreness and diarrhoea.
Review hand-foot symptoms, tablet adherence, held doses, interactions and whether the patient can continue oral treatment safely.
INR when indicated, especially with warfarin; confirm the anticoagulation monitoring plan.
ongoing: Disease assessment and scans follow the indication-specific consultant plan; no universal scan interval is imposed.
Review benefit, treatment burden, patient priorities and unresolved toxicity before continuing or changing treatment.
priority_toxicities: Severe early toxicity, including DPD-related toxicity
urgent_review_signals: Stop capecitabine and contact oncology for significant diarrhoea, painful mouth or hand-foot symptoms affecting activity, vomiting that prevents drinking, fever or sudden illness. Do not restart after a toxicity interruption until the team advises.

administration.cycle_and_sequence: capecitabine twice daily on Days 1–14, then no capecitabine on Days 15–21. Follow your individual prescription.
route_and_duration: Capecitabine 1250 mg/m² twice daily on Days 1–14 every 21 days.
practical_workflow: Confirm the aim, likely course length, blood-test arrangements and a working urgent contact number. DPD testing is required before starting the fluoropyrimidine unless already completed.

Use the prescribed morning and evening dose within 30 minutes after food on the agreed treatment days. Do not make up a missed or vomited dose. Follow the team’s hold instructions for significant diarrhoea, mouth soreness or painful hands and feet, and contact them promptly.
Ask the unit to confirm the new treatment and blood-test dates. Re-anchor supportive medicines to the treatment actually given; do not take an extra or catch-up anticancer dose yourself.
Follow your oncology unit’s urgent advice for fever, infection, severe diarrhoea, chest pain or difficulty breathing. Bring your treatment card and current medicines list.
observation_and_access: No ambulatory fluorouracil pump is used in these regimens.
Provide the local stop-and-call pathway and confirm understanding by teach-back.

evidence_at_a_glance.population: X-ACT randomised 1,987 patients after surgery for stage III colon cancer. It compared 24 weeks of capecitabine with bolus fluorouracil/folinic acid.
